question: On 2 June 2023, the EIC artificial intelligence (AI) platform for applications to the EIC Accelerator was disrupted because of a contractual dispute. Several companies reported a different method of evaluation being in the Horizon 2027 programme than in Horizon 2020, which had an adverse impact on the expected results of their projects. 1.
Is there any clarification regarding the incorrect impacts calculated in the evaluation process and the urgent and routine remedies undertaken?
Does the Commission intend to seek compensation for the platform malfunctions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) 1. On 2 June 2023, the European Innovation Council (EIC) Artificial Intelligence (AI) Platform for applying to the EIC Accelerator was no longer accessible due to a contractual dispute.

As an emergency measure, the European Innovation Council and Small and Mediumsized Enterprises Executive Agency (EISMEA) and the Commission restructured the EIC Accelerator application and migrated to the Electronic Submission System hosted on the EU Corporate Funding and Tender opportunities portal (F&T Portal)1 for full proposals. This ensured that applicants were able to continue submitting proposals.

While the F&T Portal was open with immediate effect for EIC Accelerator full (Step 2) applications, a bespoke solution was also quickly developed for EIC Accelerator short (Step 1) applications which resulted in a short disruption of a month for some applicants, but in the medium term, it ensured a more efficient application process.

The solution addressed some areas for improvement recommended by the EIC Board in their statement from March 20232 concerning mainly the reduction in the length of proposals. Other changes and improvements were being gradually introduced. For example, the Step 1 applications had been moved to the corporate tool as of 1 January 2024.

The impact of this change in platform was also subdued by a number of measures such as extensions of submission deadlines and additional trainings. Overall, the evaluation methodology remained unaffected3. 2. A legal procedure to solve the contractual dispute on the closing of the AI platform is currently pending to find a solution to this issue.

1 https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/home 2 https://eic.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2023-04/EIC_BoardStatement_AI_Platform_Final%202023.pdf 3 The submission and evaluation of proposals in the F&T portal was designed to provide similar conditions in

terms of structure and content to the previous platform and included improvements as requested by the EIC Board. All previous related materials were made available to the evaluators to carry out their evaluations. The evaluators assessed the proposals based on the same evaluation criteria. A higher flexibility was provided concerning the applicable rules of submission.
The eligibility period was extended until the end of the year (2023) for all the applicants that were eligible when the disruption of the EIC platform occurred.
